name: Saint Barthélemy
rule: The current territorial Environment Code, consolidated after 12 March 2026, restricts living specimens under Article 32-17; its plant annex concerns living plants, fruiting bodies and propagules. That invasive-species restriction does not establish a permit duty for manufactured, non-living sencha. Separate national plant-health controls still apply through Code rural L272-11-1; the applicable finished-tea import schedule has not been established. Organic Law 2007-223 Article 18 IX preserves applicable pre-2007 provisions and substitutes the new territorial references. This supplies a continuity basis for inherited national schedules, whose finished-tea list-based treatment does not itself require a new tea-specific ruling.
personalMailApplicability: The continuity of national scheduled rules does not by itself resolve any inherited local personal-import restriction. The exact scope of the 1996 Guadeloupe order for a paid private postal purchase remains unverified.
authority: Saint Barthélemy territorial government/ATE; French Code rural and plant-health authority
remainingQuestion: Actual scope and continued application of Guadeloupe Order 96-323, rather than absence of a newly issued tea-specific national schedule.
researchAttempts: Reviewed ATE territorial invasive-plant rules, native-flora guidance and plant authorization forms; no processed-tea or personal-post provision found.

Second review searched 2025/2026 local tea exclusions. The 2025 ministry overseas instruction explicitly excludes Saint Barthélemy/Saint Martin regulations from its analysis; it does not extend a mainland exemption.

Retrieved the official 199-page Environment Code via the territorial website’s March 2026 consolidation link. Read Articles 32-1 to 32-28 and the Article 32-17 plant annex: the invasive-species prohibition concerns living specimens. Separately read current Code rural L272-1, L272-3 and L272-11-1. Environmental scope is now clear but does not establish the applicable national agricultural import schedule; no inferred blanket tea ban or clearance.

2026-09-30 bounded independent French-territory peer review: Organic Law 2007-223 Article 18 IX expressly retains non-contrary pre-existing legislative and regulatory provisions and substitutes territorial references. This supplies a continuity chain for the national 1990/2006 rules after detachment from Guadeloupe, reinforced by current Code rural L272-11-1. The complete applicable national certificate schedules do not list finished tea; the 2026 Environment Code living-specimen rule does not cover non-living finished tea. However, the same continuity mechanism can preserve an applicable Guadeloupe local 1996 restriction. Its original territorial and channel scope has not been recovered.
permitFreeReason: Actual scope and continued application of Guadeloupe Order 96-323, rather than absence of a newly issued tea-specific national schedule.

name: Saint Martin (French part)
rule: Saint Martin is outside the EU plant-health territory. A Dutch NPPO country sheet lists specific dried plant goods needing certification, but does not list tea and dates its substantive rules to 2012; that cannot verify the present Japanese postal route. Current Code rural L273-6-2 expressly applies the overseas plant-health framework in L271-5 to L271-8 to Saint Martin; this confirms the governing framework but does not supply the missing commodity-level finished-tea decision. Organic Law 2007-223 Article 18 IX preserves applicable pre-2007 provisions and substitutes the new territorial references. This supplies a continuity basis for inherited national schedules, whose finished-tea list-based treatment does not itself require a new tea-specific ruling.
personalMailApplicability: The continuity of national scheduled rules does not by itself resolve any inherited local personal-import restriction. The exact scope of the 1996 Guadeloupe order for a paid private postal purchase remains unverified.
authority: Netherlands NVWA country requirements for Saint Martin; French plant-health law
remainingQuestion: Actual scope and continued application of Guadeloupe Order 96-323; the old NVWA sheet alone does not answer that local-law issue.
researchAttempts: Reviewed the full NVWA Saint Martin country sheet, including its 2012/2013 revision history and third-country plant-product list; searched French local import guidance. Current tea-specific scope remains unverified.

Second review searched 2025/2026 local tea exclusions. The 2025 ministry overseas instruction explicitly excludes Saint Barthélemy/Saint Martin regulations from its analysis; it does not extend a mainland exemption.

Read current Code rural L273-1 to L273-7, including L273-6-2’s express extension of the overseas plant-health framework. This strengthens the legal-framework evidence but is not a tea-specific schedule or a personal-post exemption.

2026-09-30 bounded independent French-territory peer review: Organic Law 2007-223 Article 18 IX supplies express continuity and territorial-reference substitution for pre-existing Guadeloupe rules; the official October 2025 Guide de legistique confirms this rule for Saint-Martin. Current Code rural L273-6-2 additionally applies the overseas framework. This is a legal chain for using inherited national schedules, not a mainland-EU substitution. Those list-based rules do not require a tea-specific permission simply because the territory changed status. The same continuity can preserve the local 1996 Guadeloupe restriction, whose original territory/channel scope remains unrecovered.
permitFreeReason: Actual scope and continued application of Guadeloupe Order 96-323; the old NVWA sheet alone does not answer that local-law issue.

name: French Guiana
rule: Guyane Order R03-2021-04-26-00003 Article 1 prohibits personal introduction/importation from all origins in any quantity using the 1990 Article 1 definitions. It is not limited to goods in the national certificate schedules. Article 2 permits derogation only following prior study. Whether steaming/manufacturing removes retail sencha from the unprocessed/simply-prepared product definition remains unresolved.
personalMailApplicability: The order covers personal introduction/importation broadly, not merely a passenger allowance; no postal exemption established.
authority: Guyane prefecture/DGTM; French Ministry of Agriculture
remainingQuestion: Whether manufacture by steaming and drying goes beyond the incorporated unprocessed/simply-prepared definition; a legal processing exclusion or authoritative general-category interpretation would settle it, without needing a bespoke tea permit.
researchAttempts: Read the 1990 overseas rule and 2025 ministry instruction retaining pre-2019 law pending an overseas decree. Located the official 2021 personal-import order; the official PDF was inaccessible, so checked its reproduced legal text (articles 1–2) against the official indexed title and number. No 2025/2026 processed-tea exemption found.

2026-09-30 bounded independent French-territory peer review: Rechecked the reproduced operative Article 1 of Order R03-2021-04-26-00003 against its official title/index. It applies the 1990 Article 1 definitions to personal imports from all origins in any quantity; it does not limit itself to Annex IV certificate-listed goods. Article 2 requires prior study for a derogation. Consequently the national exhaustive schedule cannot itself clear this personal import. Direct official PDF retrieval again closed the connection; the operative wording remains a legal-text reproduction, not an independently downloaded official copy.
permitFreeReason: Whether manufacture by steaming and drying goes beyond the incorporated unprocessed/simply-prepared definition; a legal processing exclusion or authoritative general-category interpretation would settle it, without needing a bespoke tea permit.

name: Martinique
rule: Martinique DAAF expressly cites the 22 November 2004 order prohibiting personal plant-product imports from all origins, using the 1990 definition of unprocessed or simply prepared material. The effect on factory-steamed/dried sencha is not explicitly resolved; the Réunion-specific dried-tea rule is not applied here.
personalMailApplicability: The local rule concerns personal introductions/imports generally; no manufactured-tea postal exception established.
authority: Martinique DAAF; French Ministry of Agriculture
remainingQuestion: Actual Order 043448 of 22 November 2004 and any binding processing exclusion relevant to steamed/dried manufactured tea. Do not demand a tea-specific ruling if a general category provision resolves the same question.
researchAttempts: Reviewed the DAAF controlled-goods FAQ expressly citing the 2004 personal-import ban, the 1990 product definition and the ministry’s 2025 transitional-law instruction. Searched current local processing exclusions without finding a finished-tea ruling.

2026-09-30 bounded independent French-territory peer review: Current DAAF guidance expressly describes the 22 November 2004 local restriction as applying to personal introductions/imports using the 1990 Article 1 product definition, not merely the national certificate schedule. National-list absence therefore does not settle the separate ban. The original local order was not recovered.
permitFreeReason: Actual Order 043448 of 22 November 2004 and any binding processing exclusion relevant to steamed/dried manufactured tea. Do not demand a tea-specific ruling if a general category provision resolves the same question.
